comments.author: @upgrba24
comments.text:
In 1858 the world's first commercial oil well was driled in the town of Oil Springs in Southwest Ontario.

In 1862 the first oil well gusher in Canada was drilled in the area and produced 3,000 barrels a day.

There are still oil wells in the area using 1860s technology to produce a total of 24,000 barrels a year but obviously the Canadian oil industry like the American oil industry moved on to other places in the west to exploit vast, easily accessible sources of oil.

Today few people think about Ontario or Pennsylvania when they think of oil.

replies.author: @GeographyEffect
replies.text: That’s a great parallel. Oil Springs and Pennsylvania both show how the geographic center of an industry can move far from where its earliest production began.
